item.title: AI Engineer Role Focused on LangChain, RAG, and Model Context Protocols
item.description:
AI Engineer Role Focused on LangChain, RAG, and Model Context Protocols

A pioneer in smart connected technology, precision agriculture, and autonomous machinery is opening a 12‑month contract for an AI Engineer to join its Enterprise Data Science & AI Enablement team.

🔍 Overview

  • The position is centered on translating departmental AI use cases into scalable, reusable AI agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections, Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, and modular starter kits.

⚙️ Role & Responsibilities

  • Architect, build, and maintain a central repository of reusable AI skills, agentic workflows, prompt templates, and developer starter kits.
  • Build and deploy functional AI agents, tool‑calling chains, and conversational copilots using Python and frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen.
  • Implement and standardize Model Context Protocols (MCPs) and custom tool harnesses to connect large language models (LLMs) securely with internal databases, APIs, and document stores.
  • Design and optimize RAG pipelines, embedding strategies, semantic search indices, and vector‑database storage for contextual reasoning.
  • Partner with embedded AI coaches across departments to package one‑off solutions into reusable, well‑documented enterprise knowledge assets.
  • Establish automated testing harnesses, evaluate agent performance and output quality, track adoption metrics, and manage version‑controlled releases via GitHub.

📍 Location & Work Structure

  • Locations: Austin, TX 78704; Chicago, IL; Urbandale, IA – open to 100 % fully remote work.
  • Shift: First Shift, standard daytime business hours (≈ 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM), Monday through Friday.

💰 Compensation & Contract

  • Pay Rate: $56.00 – $60.00 per hour on a W‑2 basis.
  • Contract Duration: 12 months with the possibility of extension.
  • Seniority Level: Mid‑Senior.
  • Employment Type: Full‑time.
  • Industries: Motor Vehicle Manufacturing, Industrial Machinery Manufacturing, and Manufacturing.

🛠️ Required Skills & Technologies

  • 4 + years of software/data engineering experience with generative AI systems, conversational agents, or LLM‑powered applications.
  • Expert‑level Python development and familiarity with standard data/AI libraries.
  • Hands‑on experience orchestrating LLMs using LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, AutoGen, or comparable agent frameworks.\n- Practical understanding of Model Context Protocols (MCPs), API tool calling, and dynamic context injection.
  • Experience building end‑to‑end RAG pipelines and working with vector databases such as Pinecone, Milvus, Chroma, Weaviate, Qdrant, or pgvector.
  • Advanced GitHub workflow, CI/CD automation, and test‑harness engineering.
  • Cloud engineering experience on AWS (Bedrock, SageMaker, Lambda, S3).
  • Experience with complex multi‑agent systems, big‑data platforms (Databricks, Spark, Delta Lake), and developer documentation.

📅 Application Process

  • A mandatory Glider AI/Coding assessment must be completed before client submission.
  • Interested candidates should contact the recruiter at jevin@cube-hub.com.

#AIEngineering #LangChain #RAG #EnterpriseAI

Source: AI Engineer – Enterprise AI Enablement, Agents and MCPs (LangChain & RAG at Cube Hub Inc. — Austin, TX | LinkedIn Jobs Source: Apply for Agentic AI Engineer - Rapid Prototyping in North London, London | Gumtree

item.title: Shifting AI Economics from Consumption Pricing to Infrastructure Ownership
item.description:
Shifting AI Economics from Consumption Pricing to Infrastructure Ownership

As AI transitions from experimental pilots to production portfolios, enterprises are evaluating whether to continue using consumption-based pricing or treat AI infrastructure as a productive asset.

🔍 Overview

AI is moving into production portfolios comprising assistants, agentic applications, and retrieval-and-knowledge systems. According to Deloitte’s 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise, worker access to AI rose 5% in 2025, and the number of companies with at least 40% of their AI projects in production is expected to double within six months.

⚙️ Key details

While consumption pricing provides flexibility and limits commitment, it can create variable monthly costs that are difficult to forecast as workloads and model requirements change. Organizations face a “crossover point” where owning capacity becomes more economical than buying it one request at a time.

Factors influencing this crossover point include:

  • The models being used
  • Balance of input and output tokens
  • Performance requirements
  • System design
  • Energy costs
  • The required operating model

🧩 How it works

Different AI workloads create distinct cost profiles:

Workload Type Cost Profile Characteristics
Retrieval-heavy knowledge systems May process far more context for every interaction compared to simple assistants
Agentic workflows May involve repeated reasoning, retrieval, model calls, and tool use for a single business task

When multiple workloads share infrastructure, enterprises can spread fixed costs across more productive use to improve the economics of ownership.

💡 Why it matters

Moving toward owned capacity allows a business to manage AI as a strategic infrastructure investment rather than a fluctuating monthly spend. However, this requires an operating model to ensure capacity creates value by:

  • Bringing users and workloads on board quickly
  • Governing AI use
  • Reviewing utilization
  • Identifying underutilized capacity
  • Continually identifying high-value use cases

#AIEconomics #EnterpriseAI #AIInfrastructure #CloudComputing

Source: Making AI an asset, not an expense

item.title: Apple Plans Return to Server Market With Potential Nvidia Partnership
item.description:
Apple Plans Return to Server Market With Potential Nvidia Partnership

Apple is planning to re-enter the server market, potentially partnering with Nvidia to develop the new hardware.

🔍 Overview

Apple previously retired its Xserve line in 2011 and has since left enterprise machines to other manufacturers. This new move follows the popularity of the Mac Mini and Mac Studio among AI developers, which has resulted in shortages.

⚙️ Key details

  • Hardware: The servers may run on two or four M8 Ultra chips, depending on the model.
  • Technology: The servers could incorporate Nvidia’s NVLink Fusion technology, which allows multiple chips to connect and operate as one.
  • Existing Relationship: Apple recently used Nvidia chips to power its revamped Siri servers.

🚀 Availability

  • Estimated Debut: The product is unlikely to debut until 2029.
  • Chip Timeline: The M8 line is considered a ways out, as Apple only announced the M6 in August.

#Apple #Nvidia #EnterpriseHardware #AIServers

Source: Apple might make servers again to cash in on the AI rush

item.title: Organizations define new specialized roles to secure AI platforms and manage cyber risks
item.description:
Organizations define new specialized roles to secure AI platforms and manage cyber risks

Organizations are establishing new technical roles to manage the intersection of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity, focusing on secure platform design and threat mitigation. These positions address emerging risks in generative AI, cloud infrastructure, and critical industrial systems.

🔍 Overview

The scope of these responsibilities spans from executive leadership to specialized engineering, covering cloud-based Data and AI/ML services, on-premises environments, and operational technology (OT).

🧩 How it works

Role Primary Functions
AI & Security Architect Design secure AI agent platforms, including tools, memory, and models; define controls for sandboxing and human approvals.
GenAI CBRNE Cyber Security Expert Red-team AI models for industrial systems and test safeguards against jailbreaks and adversarial prompts.
Senior Lead Security Engineer – Google Cloud Secure cloud-based Data and AI/ML services and guide engineering teams on security requirements.
Manager Cyber Cloud Security and AI Lead client projects on AI security strategy, governance, and regulatory requirements.
Cyber Engineering Manager Oversee AI/ML-based threat detection and lead security research for Navy cyber-physical systems.

⚙️ Key details

Professional responsibilities within these new frameworks include:

  • Defining security controls for sensitive data, credentials, and agent actions.
  • Managing emerging threats, including post-quantum risks.
  • Assessing vulnerabilities in Kubernetes, CI/CD, and serverless workloads.
  • Monitoring endpoint threats across Windows, macOS, Linux, and VDI environments.
  • Investigating incidents and strengthening detection across Microsoft 365, Azure, and AWS.
  • Designing cyber assessments for DoW programs to identify mission impacts.

💡 Why it matters

These specialized roles are designed to prevent information disclosure and misuse of AI models while ensuring that critical infrastructure and data protection standards are maintained as AI technologies are integrated into enterprise backend services.

#CyberSecurity #AISecurity #GenAI #CloudSecurity #RiskManagement

Source: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: September 15, 2026 - Help Net Security
